notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood for embedding a low-latency IDE copilot into SharpStream Editor. Primary constraint is Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and UI jitter under heavy local editing rhythms.

Customer goals:
- TTFT target: 80-150ms for initial first token in cold-path when using hosted API + CDN; sub-50ms preferred for warm path on dedicated pools.
- Jitter: keep per-token inter-arrival jitter < 20ms (per UI frame budget) to avoid cursor/typing stutter.
- Backpressure: graceful degradation when token budget exhausted, show partial completion + continue streaming once budget cleared.
- Token budget tuning: 200-400 token soft budget per completion by default, dynamic increase for large refactors, workspace-level budget tracking.
- Model/version pinning: must be able to pin to a deterministic model version for reproducibility across releases; preference for a quantized gpt-4o-small variant for client-side latency.

Notes from calls:
- 2026-02-18 initial scoping call (see ff-2026-02-18-9843): CTO "We need output to feel instant — users notice any micro-pauses." Wants per-keystroke partial streaming.
- 2026-03-04 bench review with SE Liam: measured cold TTFT 220ms on baseline hosted config; acceptable only with dedicated pool and prefix cache.
- Security: requires SSO (SAML) and audit logs for PR generation events; legal asked about retention and residency for EU customers.

Technical constraints and asks:
- Must support continuous streaming with partial tokens emitted at sub-50ms intervals on warm paths.
- Need API controls to enforce backpressure: aserver-side token budget and a client-visible remaining_budget field to drive UI affordances.
- Prefers automatic prefix/KV caching and low-latency routing to nearest region; want an option to prefer lower-cost fallback models only when user-acceptable quality degrade threshold reached.
- Ask for SDK samples that implement token-budget-aware UI (pause/resume, estimate remaining tokens, soft-truncate).

Why Redwood: likes unified interface for hosted/dedicated/private. If TTFT/ jitter improvements are achievable in POC, procurement early Q2.

Internal decision makers: CTO Elena Park (technical lead), Head of Product Mateo Ruiz (UX owner), Eng Manager Priya Nair (performance owner).

Quote: "If we can get TTFT under 120ms reliably and avoid stutter, adoption in our pro-tier will spike." — Mateo Ruiz

Reference artifacts: POC test harness (drive://SharpStream/POC-latency-runbook.docx), initial pricing ask (drive://SharpStream/Redwood-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf).
